questions.q:
The product formed in the following reaction.

is:
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The given reaction is the addition of HBr to an alkene in the presence of benzoyl peroxide. This proceeds via a free-radical mechanism (Kharasch effect or anti-Markovnikov addition).

First, the peroxide initiates the reaction to generate a bromine radical (Br^{\bullet}$).

The $Br^{\bullet}$ radical attacks the double bond to form the most stable carbon radical intermediate. There are two possible sites for the attack on the $HO-C_6H_4-CH=CH-CH_3$ molecule:
1. Attack at the \alpha$-carbon gives a secondary alkyl radical: $HO-C_6H_4-CH(Br)-\dot{C}H-CH_3$
2. Attack at the $\beta$-carbon gives a benzylic radical: $HO-C_6H_4-\dot{C}H-CH(Br)-CH_3$

The benzylic radical is significantly more stable due to resonance delocalization with the benzene ring (further enhanced by the electron-donating $-OH$ group). Therefore, the $Br^{\bullet}$ radical preferentially adds to the $\beta$-carbon.

The stable benzylic radical then abstracts a hydrogen atom from another HBr molecule to yield the final product:
$HO-C_6H_4-CH_2-CH(Br)-CH_3$

Note that the phenolic $-OH$ group does not react with HBr because the aryl $C-O$ bond has partial double-bond character due to resonance and is difficult to break.

Comparing this with the given options, the correct structure is represented in option (C).

Answer:
